subject: Cloud Computing
title: Total Cost of Ownership
description: Learn Total Cost of Ownership in one minute.

hook.text: A company compares cloud pricing to buying servers. The cloud looks expensive — until you count everything.

buildup.text: Total cost of ownership includes hardware, power, cooling, space, staffing, and maintenance. Servers need all of it.

discovery.text: Cloud eliminates most of those costs. No building, no power bills, no hardware replacement cycles.

twist.text: But cloud adds new costs: training, migration, and the constant operational overhead of managing cloud services.

climax.text: TCO depends on scale. For small teams, cloud wins. For massive operations, owning hardware can be cheaper.

punchline.text: Cloud isn't always cheaper. But TCO reveals the real price.

quiz.question: What does Total Cost of Ownership include beyond just hardware?
options: Power, cooling, staffing, space, maintenance, and operational overhead
Only the purchase price of servers and networking equipment
The cost of internet service for accessing cloud applications

details.summary: Total cost of ownership accounts for all costs of running a workload including compute, storage, networking, staff, licensing, training, and migration. A fair cloud TCO analysis must include on-premises costs like power, space, and personnel that are often overlooked.
details.whyItMatters: Comparing only sticker prices between cloud and on-prem is misleading. TCO provides the complete picture needed for sound financial decisions about where to run workloads.
takeaways: TCO includes all direct and indirect costs of running a workload
On-premises TCO must include power, space, and staff costs
Cloud TCO must include egress, support, and training costs

faq.question: What is typically included in a cloud TCO analysis?
faq.answer: Compute, storage, networking, data transfer, support plan, monitoring tools, training, migration costs, and staffing for cloud operations. A thorough analysis also includes the opportunity cost of engineering time spent on infrastructure versus product development.

faq.question: How do you calculate on-premises TCO fairly?
faq.answer: Include hardware purchase and refresh cycles, data center space and power, cooling costs, network equipment, software licenses, operations staff salaries, and the time cost of procurement and provisioning that cloud eliminates.
